profile.summaryBn: The country's largest Islamist political party, established in its present form in 1979. Since the 2026 election it has been the main opposition party in Parliament.
originBn: The party's origin is the Jamaat-e-Islami founded by Syed Abul A'la Maududi in 1941. In 1971 its predecessor, Jamaat-e-Islami Pakistan, opposed the independence of Bangladesh and sided with the Pakistani forces. When religion-based politics was banned after independence, its leaders and activists were for a time associated with the Islamic Democratic League; on 27 May 1979 the party emerged under the name Bangladesh Jamaat-e-Islami at Hotel Eden in Dhaka, with Abbas Ali Khan as acting Ameer.

The party took part in the 1990 mass uprising and in the movement demanding a caretaker government; in 2001 two of its leaders became ministers in the BNP-led four-party alliance government. After 2009 several of its top leaders were tried in 1971 war crimes cases, in 2013 a High Court verdict declared its registration illegal, and on 1 August 2024 the government banned the party. After the July uprising the ban was lifted on 28 August 2024, and following an Appellate Division verdict on 1 June 2025 its registration and its scales symbol were restored.
